key_insight: HA-DSB improves PET-guided whole-body MRI translation by adapting to heterogeneous anatomy and lesion regions with region-specific and lesion-aware diffusion guidance.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help shorten PET-MR scan workflows by generating higher-quality MRI-like images across the whole body, especially in lesion areas.
method: Uses a diffusion Schrödinger bridge to model image translation as stochastic transport between source and target MRI distributions.
Adds region context embeddings from a vision-language model to handle different anatomical zones across the body.
Integrates PET-derived lesion-aware guidance in both forward noise modulation and reverse attention to better preserve pathology.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior translation quality across multiple body regions and improved lesion-area results under PET guidance in whole-body MRI translation experiments.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on accurate PET inputs and robust region/lesion alignment, which may be challenging in real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Heterogeneity-Adaptive Diffusion Schrodinger Bridge for PET-Guided Whole-Body MRI Translation
